- Rationale: Stereotyped episodes, preserved awareness, episode duration 30 sec–5 min — typical for focal aware motor seizures arising from motor cortex or adjacent regions.
- Tests to confirm: Urgent scalp/video EEG (capture events), brain MRI epilepsy protocol, basic metabolic panel and glucose.

2) Focal seizures with brief automatisms (temporal/frontal lobe)
- Rationale: Focal seizures can present with repetitive purposeless movements (automatisms); awareness may be preserved or only minimally impaired. Temporal lobe events can be subtle and prolonged.
- Tests to confirm: Video-EEG, MRI brain, neuro exam, consider neuropsych testing if recurrent.

- Rationale: PNES can preserve awareness and be stereotyped; durations can be minutes. Lack of postictal confusion supports this, though PNES often have variable semiology and may be triggered by stress (patient did not recall triggers).
- Tests to confirm: Video-EEG to demonstrate absence of ictal epileptiform activity during events, psychiatric evaluation.

- Rationale: Paroxysmal involuntary movements (dystonia, chorea, ballism) can be stereotyped and last seconds to minutes with preserved awareness; often no EEG correlate.
- Tests to confirm: Neurologic exam during/after events, video-EEG (to exclude epilepsy), genetic testing if recurrent and family history, review of triggers.
